title: Git Commands & Internal Architecture
description: Beginner-to-advanced Git reference covering the object database, refs, index, commits, branches, merging, rebasing, remotes, refspecs, undo, reflog recovery, worktrees, hooks, signing, security, and collaborative workflows.

sections.title: Mental Model & Object Database
sections.description: Git stores immutable content-addressed objects and moves lightweight references through a directed acyclic commit graph.

subtopics.title: Snapshots and the Three Trees
subtopics.description: Most commands move content among HEAD, the index, and the working tree. A commit records a complete project snapshot, reusing unchanged objects.

table.title: Git State Areas
rows: Snapshot named by the current commit
Proposed contents of the next commit
Working-tree paths absent from the index

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  WT["Working tree"] -- "git add" --> IDX["Index / staging area"]
  IDX -- "git commit" --> HEAD["HEAD commit"]
  HEAD -- "git restore --source" --> WT
  HEAD -- "git restore --staged" --> IDX

subtopics.title: Blobs, Trees, Commits & Tags
subtopics.description: A blob stores file content, a tree maps names to blobs or subtrees, a commit points to a root tree and parent commits, and an annotated tag points to another object with metadata.

codeBlocks.code:
git cat-file -t HEAD
git cat-file -p HEAD
git ls-tree -r HEAD
git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}
git count-objects -vH

callouts.title: Object IDs Cover Content
callouts.text: Changing an object changes its hash. Commit identity includes the tree, parents, author/committer data, and message—not just the file diff shown by Git.

subtopics.title: Refs, HEAD & Revision Syntax
subtopics.description: Branches and tags are names stored under refs. HEAD normally symbolically names the checked-out branch; detached HEAD points directly to a commit.

codeBlocks.code:
git symbolic-ref --short HEAD
git show-ref --heads --tags
git rev-parse main~2       # first-parent ancestor
git rev-parse merge^2      # merge commit's second parent
git log main..feature      # reachable from feature, not main
git log main...feature     # symmetric difference

callouts.title: Detached HEAD Is Not Data Loss
callouts.text: Commits made while detached are valid objects. Create a branch with git switch -c <name> before the commits become difficult to find through reflogs.

sections.title: Working Tree, Index & Commits
sections.description: Build focused commits by inspecting both unstaged and staged changes before recording history.

subtopics.title: Inspect and Stage Intent
subtopics.description: Use path and patch staging to make the index match one coherent change, even when the working tree contains unrelated edits.

codeBlocks.code:
git status --short --branch
git diff --check
git add -p
git diff --staged --stat
git diff --staged

callouts.title: Review the Index, Not Just the Working Tree
callouts.text: The staged diff is the exact proposed commit. Check it for secrets, generated artifacts, debug output, accidental formatting, and incomplete tests.

subtopics.title: Commit, Amend, Fixup & Autosquash
subtopics.description: Amend replaces the current commit. Fixup commits preserve reviewable work-in-progress and can be autosquashed before sharing.

codeBlocks.code:
git commit -m "fix: preserve cancellation signal"
git commit --amend --no-edit
git commit --fixup=<target-commit>
git rebase -i --autosquash <base>

callouts.title: Amend Rewrites Identity
callouts.text: Amending creates a new commit even when the message is unchanged. Avoid rewriting commits already consumed by other collaborators unless the team coordinates it.

subtopics.title: .gitignore, Attributes & File Movement
subtopics.description: .gitignore affects untracked discovery, while .gitattributes controls path-specific behavior such as line endings, diff drivers, linguist hints, and merge handling.

codeBlocks.code:
git check-ignore -v path/to/file
git rm --cached path/to/tracked-secret.env
git check-attr -a -- path/to/file
git mv old-name new-name

callouts.title: Git Detects Renames
callouts.text: A rename is inferred later from content similarity; it is not a special stored object. git mv is a convenient working-tree move plus index update.

sections.title: Branches, Merge & Rebase
sections.description: Branches are movable commit refs. Merge preserves topology; rebase copies commits onto a new base.

subtopics.title: Create, Switch, Rename & Delete Branches
subtopics.description: Prefer switch for branch movement and restore for file restoration so intent is explicit.

codeBlocks.code:
git switch -c feature/login
git switch main
git branch --show-current
git branch -m feature/auth
git branch -d feature/auth
git branch --merged main

callouts.title: Force Delete Does Not Immediately Erase Commits
callouts.text: git branch -D removes the ref. Unreferenced commits may remain recoverable through reflogs until expiration and garbage collection, but recovery is not a substitute for checking the branch first.

subtopics.title: Merge and Conflict Resolution
subtopics.description: A fast-forward only moves a ref. A true merge combines histories and may create a two-parent commit.

codeBlocks.code:
git merge --ff-only origin/main
git merge --no-ff feature/payments
git status
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
# edit and test resolved files
git add <resolved-paths>
git merge --continue
# or abandon
git merge --abort

callouts.title: Resolve Meaning, Not Markers
callouts.text: A syntactically clean conflict resolution can still violate behavior. Understand both sides, run focused tests, inspect the final staged diff, and use rerere only when repeated resolutions are trustworthy.

subtopics.title: Rebase and Interactive History Editing
subtopics.description: Rebase replays selected commits onto another base, producing new commit identities. Interactive rebase can reorder, edit, squash, fixup, reword, or drop them.

diagram.content:
gitGraph
  commit id: "A"
  commit id: "B"
  branch feature
  checkout main
  commit id: "C"
  checkout feature
  commit id: "F1"
  commit id: "F2"

codeBlocks.code:
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main
# resolve, stage, then continue
git add <resolved-paths>
git rebase --continue
# or return to the pre-rebase state
git rebase --abort

git rebase -i --rebase-merges <base>

callouts.title: Rebase Private History by Default
callouts.text: Rebasing shared commits forces collaborators to reconcile rewritten identities. Coordinate explicitly and use --force-with-lease, never an unconditional force push, when an approved remote rewrite is necessary.

sections.title: Remotes & Collaboration
sections.description: Remote-tracking refs are local observations of remote state; fetch updates them, while push asks a remote to update its refs.

subtopics.title: Fetch, Pull & Upstream Tracking
subtopics.description: Fetch is reviewable and non-integrating. Pull performs fetch followed by a configured merge or rebase.

codeBlocks.code:
git remote -v
git fetch --prune origin
git log --oneline --graph --decorate HEAD..origin/main
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/main main
git pull --ff-only

callouts.title: Choose Pull Behavior Explicitly
callouts.text: Set pull.ff or pull.rebase according to the repository workflow. fetch followed by an explicit merge or rebase is easiest to inspect when the histories diverge.

subtopics.title: Push, Refspecs & Safe Rewrites
subtopics.description: A refspec maps a local source ref to a remote destination ref. A normal push refuses non-fast-forward updates.

codeBlocks.code:
git push -u origin feature/login
git push origin local-name:remote-name
git push --delete origin obsolete-branch
git push --force-with-lease origin feature/login

callouts.title: Lease Protects Observed Remote Work
callouts.text: --force-with-lease rejects the rewrite if the remote ref no longer matches your expected value. Fetch and inspect first; a lease reduces risk but does not make rewriting shared history harmless.

subtopics.title: Forks, Reviews & Integration Policy
subtopics.description: Keep commits focused, synchronize with the target branch, and make the pull request describe behavior, risks, tests, migration, and rollback—not merely filenames.

codeBlocks.code:
git remote add upstream <canonical-url>
git fetch upstream
git rebase upstream/main
git range-diff upstream/main...HEAD@{1} upstream/main...HEAD

callouts.title: Use range-diff After Rewriting a Series
callouts.text: range-diff compares two versions of a commit series and helps reviewers confirm that a rebase or fixup did not introduce unintended semantic changes.

sections.title: Undo, Restore & Recovery
sections.description: Choose an undo command based on whether history is shared and which of HEAD, index, or working tree must change.

rows: Move branch and reshape unpublished state

codeBlocks.code:
git restore --staged path/to/file
git restore --source=HEAD -- path/to/file
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git revert <published-commit>

callouts.title: Inspect Before Destructive Restore or Reset
callouts.text: Before --hard or restoring a working-tree path, inspect status and diffs and preserve valuable work in a commit, branch, patch, or stash. Uncommitted content may have no Git recovery path.

subtopics.title: Reflog and Lost-Commit Recovery
subtopics.description: Reflogs record local ref updates and often reveal commits after resets, rebases, amendments, or branch deletion.

callouts.title: Preserve First, Then Repair
callouts.text: Create a recovery branch at the candidate commit before resetting or rebasing anything else. Verify its tree and history, then decide how to integrate it.

callouts.title: Reflog Retention Is Configurable
callouts.text: Defaults commonly expire reachable entries after 90 days and unreachable entries after 30 days, but gc.reflogExpire settings and garbage collection affect recovery. Reflogs are local and are not a backup.

subtopics.title: Stash, Clean and Bisect
subtopics.description: Stash is temporary commit-like storage, clean removes untracked files, and bisect searches history for the first bad commit.

codeBlocks.code:
git stash push -u -m "wip before upgrade"
git stash list
git stash branch recovery/stash stash@{0}

git clean -ndx  # preview ignored and untracked removal

git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good <known-good>
git bisect run ./test-regression.sh
git bisect reset

callouts.title: Preview clean Every Time
callouts.text: git clean can permanently delete untracked and ignored files. Use -n with the exact same scope first and do not treat a stash as durable backup.

sections.title: Worktrees, Automation & Security
sections.description: Use repository-level features deliberately and treat configuration, hooks, and fetched content as part of the security boundary.

subtopics.title: Worktrees and Submodules
subtopics.description: Worktrees provide multiple checkouts sharing one object database. Submodules record a specific commit from another repository and require an explicit lifecycle policy.

codeBlocks.code:
git worktree add ../project-hotfix -b hotfix origin/main
git worktree list
git worktree remove ../project-hotfix

git submodule update --init --recursive
git submodule status --recursive

callouts.title: Do Not Copy .git Internals Between Worktrees
callouts.text: Linked worktrees have administrative metadata and branch exclusivity rules. Use git worktree commands to add, move, repair, prune, and remove them.

subtopics.title: Hooks, Signing & Layered Configuration
subtopics.description: Configuration is layered across system, global, local, worktree, and command scopes. Hooks automate local policy; signed commits and tags provide verifiable authorship evidence.

codeBlocks.code:
git config --show-origin --show-scope --list
git config --local core.hooksPath .githooks
git commit -S -m "release: 2.0.0"
git log --show-signature -1
git tag -s v2.0.0 -m "Release 2.0.0"

callouts.title: Local Hooks Are Not Enforcement
callouts.text: Hooks can be bypassed and are not cloned by default. Enforce required tests, signature policy, and protected-branch rules on trusted server or CI infrastructure.

subtopics.title: Security, Maintenance & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Repository operations can execute configured tools or expose secrets through history. Review trust boundaries before running project commands or rewriting data.

codeBlocks.code:
git fsck --full
git maintenance run
git verify-commit HEAD
git verify-tag <tag>
git log --all -- path/to/suspected-secret

callouts.title: Deleting a File Does Not Remove Its History
callouts.text: Revoke exposed credentials immediately. Removing secrets from all reachable history requires a coordinated history rewrite, force updates, clone cleanup, and communication with every consumer.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Review status and staged diffs, fetch before integrating, protect shared refs, use force-with-lease only by agreement, sign releases, scan secrets, back up critical repositories, and test recovery procedures.
